world: Third-person action game, camera following just behind and above the rider the whole time. A young Black Ethiopian man in his twenties gallops a grey horse across a vast desert of red sand and black volcanic rock in the medieval Ethiopian highlands, around the twelfth century. He wears a white cotton shamma cloak with a woven red border flying behind him, a white head wrap, a leather round shield and a long spear. Ahead, a salt caravan of camels led by Black Ethiopian men in white cotton, a small rock-hewn stone church and round thatched huts on a ridge. On the horizon a low brown wall of dust is rising. Golden afternoon, wide Leone landscape, dust from the hooves, fine grain.
beats: A colossal red sandstorm, a wall of dust hundreds of metres high, rolls across the desert toward the rider, swallowing the horizon.
The sandstorm sweeps over the rider and the caravan: swirling red dust fills the whole sky and everything vanishes into orange haze except the rider's white cloak.
Deep inside the storm, tall shapes glimmer faintly through the dust ahead of the rider.

The sandstorm passes and the dust clears: the desert is now the far future. Gleaming silver towers, glass domes over a green oasis city, fields of solar mirrors, a train gliding on tall pylons across the plain; the rider gallops on toward it.

An Afrofuturist Ethiopian city rises ahead: white and copper towers carved like rock-hewn churches, banners woven with tibeb patterns, Black Ethiopian people in white cotton and silver cloth on wide terraces.
